clue.text: Half of misers' donation in doubt

indicators.note: half of the six-letter word misers keeps only its front three letters

parts.note: a donation is a giving, the act of handing something over

explanation.surface: A miser grudgingly parts with half a donation, full of reservations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' takes the first half of MISERS, giving MIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A misgiving is a feeling of doubt or apprehension, so the noun swaps directly for doubt.

clue.text: Wimps of a type very taken by politicians

indicators.note: something taken by a group is held within it, so these letters go inside the politicians' letters

parts.note: MPs are Members of Parliament
ilk means a type or kind
so means very, as in 'so tired'

explanation.surface: Weaklings of a particular sort are the ones politicians like to recruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Milksops are feeble, timid people, the same as wimps.

clue.text: Help in finding objects on a river bed

indicators.note: bed suggests the letters are bedded into the run of words that follows, embedded across them

explanation.surface: Something that assists a search of a riverbed for lost items.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a description of the gadget, and it is one, but the letters lie bedded in 'objects on a river'.
explanation.definitionFit: Echo-sounding equipment is an aid to locating submerged items, so it helps a search.

clue.text: Badges almost intended to take a hundred: that's being petty

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for badges is dropped

parts.note: insignia are badges of rank or membership

indicators.note: the intended swallows the hundred, which goes inside

parts.note: one's intended is a fiancé, the person one is engaged to
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone whose badges nearly made it, and whose fiancé wanted a hundred, is told they are being small-minded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is a link; 'intended' as a noun is the person one is engaged to.
explanation.definitionFit: Insignificance is the state of being trivial or unimportant, which is what being petty describes.

clue.text: Fashionable pen in outline

indicators.note: in says the pen's letters sit inside the other piece
out, lifted from the word outline, signals that the letters of line are put out of order

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: A stylish pen drawn in outline form.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lifts 'out' from 'outline' and uses it as the anagram signal on the rest of the word, a split solvers rarely expect.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fashionable means being in the current mode, the idiom for which is to be stylish.

clue.text: State of the world (old and new)

definitions.text: State of the world (old and new)

parts.words: State of the world (old and new)
parts.note: the name belongs both to a country in the Caucasus, in the Old World, and to a US state, in the New World

explanation.surface: A question about the condition of the planet, then and now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State of the world' reads as the condition of things; it is a state found in both the Old and New Worlds.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is shared by a Caucasus republic in the Old World and a US state in the New.

clue.text: Temper heard by the side of the road

indicators.note: heard says a word is spoken, so its sound gives the entry

parts.note: to curb is to temper or restrain

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper and is overheard at the roadside.
explanation.walkthrough: KERB is British spelling for the edge of a pavement (US curb).
explanation.definitionFit: The kerb is the raised edge where the pavement meets the roadway, at its side.

clue.text: Being naughty, entice with sex

indicators.note: naughty suggests misbehaving, so these letters behave badly and rearrange

explanation.surface: A naughty person lures someone by offering sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being naughty' reads as one phrase, but 'Being' is the definition and 'naughty' the anagram signal; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being, as a noun, is existence: the state of living or being real.

clue.text: Rupert Murdoch is old

definitions.meaning: the media owner stands ..., that is owns, a London newspaper of that name

explanation.walkthrough: Murdoch's News UK owns The Times, a British national daily, so he is literally the power behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being behind the times means being old-fashioned, and the owner of a paper stands behind it.

clue.text: Running wild isn't held in high esteem

indicators.note: held in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: admiration is high esteem

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as its letters, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A wild runaway is not someone anyone holds in high regard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' looks like part of the surface's escape; it is the definition, as in running a company.
explanation.definitionFit: The administration of a business is the running of it, its management.

clue.text: See 26
Swimmer to cross water first to end in elegant surroundings

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other, the 'surroundings'

parts.note: swish is informal for smart or elegant

indicators.note: the first letter is taken from the front and put at the end

parts.note: to ford is to cross a river through shallow water

explanation.surface: A swimmer crosses the water and finishes first in smart surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to end' turns FORD into ORDF, which goes 'in' SWISH.
explanation.definitionFit: A swordfish is a large ocean fish, so it is a swimmer.

clue.text: Thin piece of material clutched by extremely shambolic granny

indicators.note: clutched by means held inside the other letters
extremely takes the extreme letters, the first and last, of each word

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: A scrap of fabric clings to a very untidy, skinny old woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thin' is an adjective here, describing a skinny person.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraggy means lean and bony, a synonym of thin.

clue.text: First in the valley to shine

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the valley

parts.note: a glen is a valley, especially in Scotland
1st is the abbreviation for first

explanation.surface: Something comes first in the valley competition and gleams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First in' looks like an initial-letter pick; it is the ordinal 1st written out.
explanation.definitionFit: To glisten is to shine with a sparkling, wet light.

clue.text: Anti-abortion or anti-reproduction is spreading

parts.note: pro-life is the label of the anti-abortion movement

indicators.note: a reproduction remakes something, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A debate on whether opposing abortion or opposing breeding is gaining ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reproduction' rearranges OR and ANTI into RATION; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Proliferation is rapid growth or spread, and spreading is that same increase.

clue.text: Masterminded grandiose scheme

indicators.note: a scheme is a plan or arrangement, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A villain masterminded a grandiose plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something organised was arranged and directed, which is what masterminded means.

clue.text: See 8
Steer tight: one way to show determination

indicators.note: a way is a manner or arrangement, so the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to grip the steering wheel tightly as a sign of resolve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one way' reads as an example; 'one' is fodder and 'way' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To grit one's teeth is an idiom for steeling oneself and persevering, showing resolve.

clue.text: Complex part ends up ideologically reversed

indicators.note: reversed says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A complicated piece about someone who ends up turning against their ideology.
explanation.walkthrough: SUPIDEO runs across 'ends up ideologically'; 'reversed' turns it.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud's Oedipus complex is named after the Greek king, who is thus a component of that term.

clue.text: Collectively providing service in a particular direction

indicators.note: in places the service inside the direction

parts.note: ENE is the compass bearing east-north-east
Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: People together hold a church service facing one direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'providing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: En masse is French for all together, in a body, which is collectively.

clue.text: Appreciation of actor's rising moment has vanished

indicators.note: has vanished says these letters are gone from the actor's name

parts.note: Tom Hanks is a Hollywood actor

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: mo is short for moment, as in 'half a mo'

explanation.surface: Gratitude to an actor whose moment of fame has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns MO into OM, which 'has vanished' from TOMHANKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Thanks is an expression of gratitude, the same as appreciation.

clue.text: Brief reply in tough parliamentary exchanges recorded

indicators.note: in places the short reply inside the other word

parts.note: hard means tough
ANS is the short form of answer

explanation.surface: A short answer given in a fierce debate in the Commons is written down.
explanation.walkthrough: Hansard is the official verbatim record of debates in the UK Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed record of Westminster debates is named after the Hansard printing family.

clue.text: Least likely to give me an estimate, having lost one friend

indicators.note: having lost means these letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written; that the remaining letters also run forwards here is a coincidence of the deletion, not a concealed word
I is the Roman numeral one
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A stingy person refuses to give me an estimate, after losing a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: The meanest person is the stingiest, the least inclined to part with money.

clue.text: Girl's correct aspiration

definitions.note: read as 'Girl is', the 's being the link

parts.note: to edit is to correct text
an aspirate is the breathed sound H

explanation.surface: A girl's correct ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspiration' looks like ambition; in phonetics it is the breathy H sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith is a woman's first name, so a girl's name.

clue.text: Home space designed to be pretentious, isn't it?

parts.note: a nest is a home

indicators.note: designed means planned and arranged, so these letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: A designer home makes a showy impression, doesn't it?
explanation.walkthrough: N'EST-CE PAS is French for 'isn't it?', used in English as an affectation.
explanation.definitionFit: This French tag question is the counterpart of 'isn't it?', used by English speakers to sound refined.

clue.text: Moron's tail replaced by moron's head, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: replaced by says one letter is swapped out for another

parts.note: an idiot is a moron

indicators.note: head means the first letter

explanation.surface: A fool's ending is swapped for another fool's beginning, in a way of talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail' is the last letter, T, of IDIOT; 'replaced by' puts M, from 'moron's head', in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a turn of phrase, a characteristic form of expression.

clue.text: Pays less attention to face with wrinkles

parts.note: a side is a face, as of a cube
lines are wrinkles on the face

explanation.surface: Someone takes less notice of a face covered in wrinkles.
explanation.definitionFit: To sideline something is to push it to the margins, ignoring it more.

clue.text: Shank used to position these

indicators.note: to position is to set in place, so the letters are placed in a new order

explanation.surface: The leg is where these are positioned.
explanation.walkthrough: A skean-dhu is a small Highland dagger tucked into the top of the sock, against the shank or lower leg.
explanation.definitionFit: These knives are worn in the stocking against the lower leg, which the clue calls the shank.
